quests.instruction: In Ms. Ortiz's class, children counted the people who live in their homes: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 9. What does this tell us?
quests.correctAnswer: Households come in many sizes 🔢
options: Every family has exactly four people 👪
Only the biggest homes are real families 🏠
Households come in many sizes 🔢
quests.hint: Look at how different the numbers are.
quests.explanation: The numbers range from 2 to 9, which shows that families and households come in many sizes. None of them is the 'right' size.
quests.funFact: Around the world, the average household size ranges from fewer than three people in some countries to more than six in others.

quests.instruction: A class survey shows the number of people in each home: 4, 3, 4, 5, 4, 2. Which number appears most often?
quests.hint: Count how many times each number shows up.
quests.explanation: The number 4 appears three times, more than any other number, so it is the most common size in this group.
quests.funFact: The value that appears most often in a set of numbers is called the mode.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is fair to say about families?
quests.correctAnswer: Families can be big or small and loving 💛
options: A real family has two children and two adults 👪
Small families are less happy than big ones 😔
Families can be big or small and loving 💛
quests.hint: Think about what makes a family a family.
quests.explanation: Families come in many sizes and shapes, and love and care do not depend on how many people there are.
quests.funFact: Some children are the only child in their family, while others have ten or more brothers and sisters.

quests.instruction: Which statement about homes is true?
quests.correctAnswer: Families live in many kinds of homes 🏠
options: Families live in many kinds of homes 🏠
All families live in houses with gardens 🏡
Only big buildings can be a family's home 🏰
quests.hint: Think about the places your friends and relatives live.
quests.explanation: Families live in houses, apartments, farms, boats, and many other places. A home is where people care for each other.
quests.funFact: Some families live on houseboats, such as those on the canals of Amsterdam or on Dal Lake in Kashmir.

quests.instruction: What makes a place a home for a family?
quests.correctAnswer: People caring for each other there 💛
options: At least three bedrooms and a garden 🛏️
A big, expensive building in town 🏙️
People caring for each other there 💛
quests.hint: Think about what feels like home when you are away.
quests.explanation: A home is about the people and the care, not the size or the type of building.
quests.funFact: People who travel a lot, such as sailors or nomadic herders, make a home wherever their family is.

quests.instruction: Kofi lives in a tall apartment building in a city, and Mei lives on a farm. Which is a fair observation?
quests.correctAnswer: Their homes differ, and both are real homes 🏠
options: Their homes differ, and both are real homes 🏠
Kofi's city flat is better than Mei's farm 🏙️
Mei's farm is not a proper home at all 🌾
quests.hint: Different does not mean better or worse.
quests.explanation: Homes can look very different. An apartment and a farmhouse can both be warm, caring homes.
quests.funFact: More than half of the world's people now live in cities, while many others live in villages and on farms.

quests.instruction: Nilo lives with his grandmother, his aunt, and two cousins in one home. Which statement is true?
quests.correctAnswer: Many families live with relatives 🏠
options: This cannot be a real family home 🚫
Cousins always live in separate homes 🚪
Many families live with relatives 🏠
quests.hint: Think about the different ways families can live under one roof.
quests.explanation: In many families, relatives such as grandparents, aunts, and cousins share a home. This is common in many parts of the world.
quests.funFact: In many countries, living with extended family is the usual arrangement for lots of children.

quests.instruction: Yazid spends school days with his aunt near his school and holidays with his parents in another town. Which statement is true?
quests.correctAnswer: Both are places where family lives 💛
options: He is not truly part of either family 🚫
He must choose only one of the homes 🏠
Both are places where family lives 💛
quests.hint: A child can belong in more than one place.
quests.explanation: Some children live in more than one home during the year, for example because of school or family work. They belong to the whole family.
quests.funFact: In many countries, children stay with relatives near a good school or when their parents work far away.

quests.instruction: Which household has three generations living together?
quests.correctAnswer: Grandmother, her son, and his daughter 🏠
options: A mother, a father, and two young children 🏠
Grandmother, her son, and his daughter 🏠
Three cousins sharing an apartment in town 🏠
quests.hint: Generations are like the rows on a family tree.
quests.explanation: A grandmother, her son, and his daughter are three different generations in one home.
quests.funFact: Some family homes have four generations living under one roof.

quests.instruction: Gwen has curly red hair and her brother Marek has straight black hair. Are they still brother and sister?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, looks do not decide family 💛
options: No, brothers and sisters must look alike 👀
Yes, looks do not decide family 💛
Only if their hair is the same color 🎨
quests.hint: Think about what makes people siblings.
quests.explanation: Siblings can look very different. Family is about being connected and caring for each other, not about looking the same.
quests.funFact: Children in the same family can have different hair, eye, and skin colors, because they get a mix of traits from many relatives.

quests.instruction: A classmate asks Hamid, 'You don't look like your mom. Are you really her son?' What is the best reply?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Yes. Family members can look different.' 💛
options: 'Mind your own business and go away!' 😠
'I'm never going to talk to you again.' 🚫
'Yes. Family members can look different.' 💛
quests.hint: A calm, honest answer helps others learn.
quests.explanation: Family members do not always look alike. A calm answer helps other people understand.
quests.funFact: Relatives can look surprisingly different, because traits come from many ancestors, not just two.

quests.instruction: Which of these matters most in making a group of people a family?
quests.correctAnswer: Caring about each other 💛
options: All having the same hair color 💇
Caring about each other 💛
All sharing the same last name 📛
quests.hint: Which one could be true for every family?
quests.explanation: Care, commitment, and belonging are what make people a family. Looks and names can differ.
quests.funFact: Many cultures have special words for people who are family through love, not through blood.

quests.instruction: Kemi's last name is different from her mother's last name. Is that possible?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, families use names in many ways 📛
options: No, family members must share a last name 📛
Yes, families use names in many ways 📛
Only if they are not related 🚫
quests.hint: Think about how different cultures choose names.
quests.explanation: In some places children take their father's name, in others their mother's, or both, or a name made from a parent's first name. Names work differently around the world.
quests.funFact: In Spain and many Latin American countries, people usually have two last names, one from each parent.

quests.instruction: In Iceland, many people have a last name made from a parent's first name, such as 'Jónsdóttir', meaning 'Jón's daughter'. What does this show?
quests.correctAnswer: Last names can follow traditions 🌍
options: Last names can follow traditions 🌍
Everyone in Iceland must share a name 🚫
Names do not matter in families 😐
quests.hint: Compare it with last names that are handed down unchanged.
quests.explanation: In Iceland a child's last name often shows whose child they are. A brother and sister may have different last names from their parents, and that is normal there.
quests.funFact: In Iceland, phone books are often listed by first name, because last names come from a parent's first name.

quests.instruction: Valentina is meeting a new classmate and is not sure how to say his name. What is a respectful thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask how to say it, then practice 👂
options: Give him a nickname without asking 🙃
Ask how to say it, then practice 👂
Avoid using his name at all 🤐
quests.hint: Names matter to the people who carry them.
quests.explanation: Asking how to say a name shows respect, and trying to say it correctly makes people feel welcome.
quests.funFact: Many people say that hearing their name said correctly makes them feel included.

quests.instruction: Hiba speaks Arabic with her grandmother and English at school. What do we call a person who speaks two languages?
quests.correctAnswer: Bilingual 🗣️
options: Bicolor 🎨
Bilingual 🗣️
Biannual 📅
quests.hint: Look at the beginning of the word: it tells you how many.
quests.explanation: 'Bilingual' means able to speak two languages. 'Bi' means two and 'lingual' is about language.
quests.funFact: Many experts estimate that about half or more of the world's people use more than one language.

quests.instruction: Soo-jin's grandmother speaks only Korean, and her friend Tom speaks only English. How could they enjoy a visit together?
quests.correctAnswer: Use smiles, gestures, and some help 😊
options: Decide that they cannot visit 🚫
Keep shouting in their own language 📢
Use smiles, gestures, and some help 😊
quests.hint: Communication is more than words.
quests.explanation: Gestures, smiles, pictures, and some help from a translator let people share time even without a shared language.
quests.funFact: Roughly 7,000 languages are spoken in the world today.

quests.instruction: Why is it a strength when a child speaks the home language and the school language?
quests.correctAnswer: They can talk with more people 🌍
options: They can ignore what teachers say 🤫
They can talk with more people 🌍
They will never make a mistake 🙈
quests.hint: Think about all the people who can understand them.
quests.explanation: Speaking two languages lets a child connect with family and friends, and it helps keep family traditions alive.
quests.funFact: Some words travel between languages: 'pajama' comes from Hindi, 'safari' from Swahili, and 'kindergarten' from German.

quests.instruction: At school, Lia's family celebrates Eid, Tom's celebrates Christmas, and Mina's celebrates neither. What is a respectful response?
quests.correctAnswer: Be curious and kind about all of them 💛
options: Say that only one celebration is right ❌
Be curious and kind about all of them 💛
Tell Mina she has to pick a festival 🎉
quests.hint: Everyone's traditions matter to them.
quests.explanation: Families celebrate in many ways, and some do not celebrate special days. Being curious and kind makes everyone feel welcome.
quests.funFact: People around the world celebrate hundreds of different festivals, many tied to seasons, harvests, or history.

quests.instruction: Tomás wants to learn about his friend's holiday. Which question is respectful?
quests.correctAnswer: 'What do you do on that day?' 🙂
options: 'What do you do on that day?' 🙂
'Why is your holiday so weird?' 😒
'Is your family strange?' 😕
quests.hint: Ask in a way that shows interest, not judgment.
quests.explanation: Open, friendly questions show interest and help you learn without judging.
quests.funFact: Many people enjoy sharing their traditions when others ask with real curiosity.

quests.instruction: A class plans a birthday party for Dario, but his family does not celebrate birthdays. What is the best thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask Dario's family what feels right 💬
options: Hold the party and make him come 🎂
Leave him out of the class activity 🚪
Ask Dario's family what feels right 💬
quests.hint: Respect the choices that families make.
quests.explanation: Not all families celebrate birthdays. Asking what feels right lets everyone take part in a way that suits them.
quests.funFact: Different cultures mark the day someone was born in different ways, and some do not mark it at all.

quests.instruction: Zeke's sister uses a wheelchair. Which choice helps plan a family outing that includes her?
quests.correctAnswer: Pick a place with ramps or a lift ♿
options: Pick a place with ramps or a lift ♿
Pick a place with only steep stairs 🪜
Go without her and tell her later 🏠
quests.hint: Plan so that everyone can take part.
quests.explanation: Checking for ramps, lifts, and wide doors makes sure the whole family can enjoy the outing together.
quests.funFact: The wheelchair symbol is recognized in many countries as showing that a place is designed for access.

quests.instruction: Grandma Wanda uses a walker and walks slowly. What is a thoughtful way for the family to walk to the park?
quests.correctAnswer: Walk at her pace and chat 🚶
options: Walk fast and meet her at the park 🏃
Say she is too slow to join in 🚪
Walk at her pace and chat 🚶
quests.hint: Include everyone by adjusting to their needs.
quests.explanation: Walking at her pace lets her join in and gives everyone time to talk.
quests.funFact: A slower walk gives people more time to notice and enjoy what is around them.

quests.instruction: Bao's cousin has dyslexia and finds reading slow. What is a kind way to include her in a board game with reading cards?
quests.correctAnswer: Read the cards out loud together 📖
options: Read the cards out loud together 📖
Tell her she should read faster ⏩
Leave her out of the game 🚪
quests.hint: Different people need different kinds of help.
quests.explanation: Dyslexia makes reading harder, but it has nothing to do with how clever someone is. Reading the cards together lets her take part.
quests.funFact: Dyslexia is common: experts estimate that 5 to 10 percent of people have it.

quests.instruction: A friend says, 'I live with my aunt and uncle.' What is a respectful response?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Nice! What do you do together?' 🙂
options: 'But where are your real parents?' 🙄
'Oh, that is so sad for you.' 😟
'Nice! What do you do together?' 🙂
quests.hint: Do not assume how your friend feels about it.
quests.explanation: Many children live with relatives. Showing interest in the good things, and not assuming it is sad, is respectful.
quests.funFact: Children living with relatives is common, and in many places it is a normal part of family life.

quests.instruction: A classmate has two dads. Someone asks, 'Which one is your real dad?' What would be a kinder thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'What are your dads like?' 💬
options: 'What are your dads like?' 💬
'They cannot both be your real dads.' 😒
'Having two dads sounds really strange.' 😕
quests.hint: A parent is real if they take care of the child.
quests.explanation: Both dads are real parents to him. Asking kind questions that show interest respects his family.
quests.funFact: A child with two dads or two moms has the same kinds of everyday family life as other children.

quests.instruction: In art class, everyone draws their family. One friend draws herself, her grandmother, and a dog. What is a good thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I like how you drew your family.' 🎨
options: 'I like how you drew your family.' 🎨
'You forgot to draw your mom and dad.' 😟
'Your drawing is not a real family.' 🙅
quests.hint: Notice what she is proud of.
quests.explanation: Every family drawing is correct for the person who drew it. A kind comment respects her family.
quests.funFact: Teachers often invite children to draw 'the people who care for me', so that every family shape fits.

quests.instruction: Which statement about families is true?
quests.correctAnswer: Families can differ and still be loving 💛
options: There is one best kind of family 🏆
Families can differ and still be loving 💛
Families must always live in one house 🏠
quests.hint: Think about everything you have learned about homes, names, and traditions.
quests.explanation: Families differ in size, homes, names, languages, traditions, and abilities. What they share is care for each other.
quests.funFact: Researchers who study families around the world find enormous variety, and many kinds of families can nurture children well.

quests.instruction: Camille's family has five people and speaks two languages. Jomo's family has two people and eats late at night. What is true?
quests.correctAnswer: Both families have their own ways 🏠
options: Only one of them is a real family 🚫
Both families have their own ways 🏠
They cannot be good friends 🙅
quests.hint: Different does not mean wrong.
quests.explanation: Both families care for each other and have their own habits. Differences are part of what makes friendships interesting.
quests.funFact: Learning about other families can help children feel at ease with differences.

quests.instruction: Rafi's class graph shows how many people live in each home: 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 8. How many homes have 5 people?
quests.correctAnswer: 3 homes 🔢
options: 3 homes 🔢
2 homes 🔢
1 home 🔢
quests.hint: Count how many times 5 appears.
quests.explanation: The number 5 appears three times in the list, so three homes have five people.
quests.funFact: Reading lists and graphs like this is how people spot patterns about families and communities.
